draft.title: Writing a thesis statement
card: A thesis statement is a one-sentence answer to the question you have been set. It sits at the start of a historical argument.
A thesis takes a clear position. It says what you think and gives a reason in brief, so someone could disagree with it.
A thesis is not a topic, a question or a list of facts. It answers the question rather than describing the subject.
Every paragraph that follows supports the thesis with evidence. A paragraph that does not help prove the thesis does not belong.
draft.remember: A thesis answers the question with a clear position, and each paragraph backs it up with evidence.

a.q: Which is the best thesis statement for the question: Why did many people leave Britain for the Australian colonies in the 1800s?
opts: Most left because gold and cheap land promised a better life
This essay will discuss people who left Britain for Australia
Many people left Britain for the Australian colonies in 1800s
Why did so many people choose to leave Britain for Australia
a.why: The first option answers the question, takes a position and gives a reason that others could dispute. The third only states the topic as a fact and gives no reason. The second and fourth do not answer the question at all.
a.clue: Which one answers the question and gives a reason?

b.q: Priya is writing an essay arguing that the Industrial Revolution changed daily life more for factory workers than for landowners. Her thesis is clear and takes a position. What should her body paragraphs do?
opts: Each give evidence that supports her thesis
Each cover a different view and stay neutral
Each repeat the thesis in the same words
Each describe a different invention in order
b.why: Once a thesis takes a position, every paragraph must supply evidence for it. Describing inventions can seem on topic, but facts that are not used to prove the thesis do not build the argument.
b.clue: Think about what each paragraph is there to prove.
